message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020:

| # | Title | Release Date (US) | Director | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|-------------------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | 12 Feb 2020 | Leigh Whannell | A modern, psychological take on the classic horror trope, blending suspense with social commentary on abuse and gaslighting. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | 20 Mar 2020 (limited) | Guy Ritchie | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced storytelling, witty dialogue, and ensemble cast make this heist‑drama a stylish, entertaining watch. |
| 3 | **The Hunt** | 27 Apr 2020 | Thomas Vinterberg | A chilling thriller about a man falsely accused of child abuse, exploring paranoia, mob mentality, and the fragility of reputation. |
| 4 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | 11 Jun 2020 | Aaron Sorkin | Though more courtroom drama than traditional crime‑thriller, its tense narrative and historical stakes keep viewers on edge. |
| 5 | **The Irishman** | 24 Nov 2020 (Netflix) | Martin Scorsese | A sprawling, slow‑burn gangster epic that uses time‑jumping and de-aging tech to deliver a gripping, character‑driven story. |
| 6 | **The Night House** | 18 Oct 2020 (limited) | David Bruckner | A psychological thriller that blends supernatural elements with domestic tension, creating an unsettling atmosphere. |
| 7 | **The Last Duel** | 25 Nov 2020 (Netflix) | Ridley Scott | A medieval crime‑thriller that examines truth, justice, and gender dynamics through a duel‑based plot. |
| 8 | **The Little Things** | 23 Dec 2020 (limited) | John Lee Hancock | A gritty, noir‑inspired investigation into a serial killer, featuring strong performances by Denzel Washington and Rami Malek. |
| 9 | **The Devil All the Time** | 30 Nov 2020 (Netflix) | Antonio Campos | A bleak, atmospheric crime‑thriller that explores violence, faith, and morality in rural America. |
|10 | **The Woman in the Window** | 29 Oct 2020 (Netflix) | Andrew Jarecki | A psychological thriller that plays with unreliable narration and voyeuristic suspense, starring Amy Adams. |

These films cover a range of sub‑genres—from psychological thrillers and heist capers to courtroom dramas and period crime stories—making 2020 a surprisingly diverse year for crime‑thrillers. Enjoy!
